extracted.intended_audience: TeX/LaTeX/ConTeXt/plain-TeX users who create graphics with TikZ/pgf (from beginners to advanced users)
extracted.subtask_description: Authoring and styling vector graphics inside TeX documents using the TikZ/pgf system: placing drawing commands inside tikzpicture, structuring with scopes and styles, specifying coordinates, nodes, and paths, and extending coordinate systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special syntax for specifying trees
rubrics_metrics.description: A node can be followed by any number of children, each introduced by the keyword child. The children are nodes themselves, each of which may have children in turn (integrated with the special node syntax).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the child { node { ... } } constructs inside a node specification. Because trees are made from nodes you can apply node/options to style nodes and edge-from-parent options to style edges (examples show modifying every node and edge from parent styles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of graphic parameters with scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Put drawing/filling commands that should share graphic parameters in a {scope} environment that takes graphic options as an optional parameter; specified parameters apply only to commands inside the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nested {scope} environments or individual drawing commands can override outer scope parameters. The tikzpicture environment itself behaves like a scope (optional argument applies to whole picture). Example: three red lines in a [color=red] scope, etc. Use scopes to avoid repeating options and to localize clipping paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: tikzpicture is the outermost scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The outermost scope of TikZ is the {tikzpicture} environment. You may give drawing commands only inside this environment; giving them outside will result in chaos. All graphic options are local to the {tikzpicture}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands like \path are only defined inside tikzpicture. When the environment is processed the contents are put into a box; non-pgf commands should not produce output. Use the optional argument of tikzpicture to set picture-wide options. Plain TeX and ConTeXt provide analogous environment commands (starttikzpicture/stop).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounding box and [use as bounding box] recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: pgf guesses a bounding box by updating it for every coordinate encountered; line thickness and Bezier control points are not considered and can make the bounding box inaccurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the bounding box is too large or otherwise inaccurate (e.g., control points lie far outside the curve), use the [use as bounding box] option to set an explicit bounding box.

rubrics_metrics.name: baseline option for tikzpicture
rubrics_metrics.description: baseline=(dimension or coordinate) influences the baseline of the resulting picture: normally the lower end is put on the baseline; baseline specifies which picture y-coordinate should align with the text baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can give a dimension (e.g., baseline=0pt) or a coordinate (baseline=(X.base)) so the baseline is set to that coordinate's y at the end of the picture. Useful for inline graphics. If omitted, 0pt is assumed. Examples show inline arrow and node alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: execute at begin picture / execute at end picture
rubrics_metrics.description: Options execute at begin picture=(code) and execute at end picture=(code) install code to be executed at the beginning/end of the picture; they must be given in the optional argument of tikzpicture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: execute at end picture accumulates if used multiple times. These options are mainly used in styles like every picture to run initialization or cleanup code (example fills a background rectangle in a background layer at end).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global picture options via style=every picture / \tikzstyle{every picture}
rubrics_metrics.description: All options end at the end of the picture; to set an option globally use the style every picture (e.g., \tikzstyle{every picture}=[semithick]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures options are installed at the beginning of each picture. Use the appropriate command for LaTeX, plain TeX, or ConTeXt forms of the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the \tikz command for small inline graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: The \tikz[(options)]{commands} shorthand places commands inside a tikzpicture and adds a semicolon; intended for small graphics only and the commands may not contain a paragraph (no empty line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the text after \tikz does not start with an opening brace, the next semicolon ends the tikz text. Use this for small inline shapes; for larger pictures use the tikzpicture environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: By default pictures are transparent (no background). Background styles are provided in the pgflibrarytikzbackgrounds library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want colored backgrounds, frames, or decorations use the backgrounds library (Section 20) rather than requiring backgrounds by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope environment for structuring pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside tikzpicture you can create scopes using \begin{scope}[(options)] ... \end{scope}. Options are local to the environment and clipping paths are also local (clipping ends at scope end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: style=every scope is installed at each scope start. execute at begin scope / execute at end scope options install code local to the current scope (effects do not apply to subscopes). Plain TeX and ConTeXt have analogous scope commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping inside paths
rubrics_metrics.description: The \path command takes graphic options that are local to the path; you can create local scopes within a path by using curly braces, e.g., { [rounded corners] -- ... }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many options apply only to the path as a whole and cannot be scoped this way (for example, the color of the path cannot be scoped). Elements inside a path argument (like nodes) may take local options that apply only to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using styles to manage appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: A style is a predefined set of graphic options. Use style=(style name) to invoke it. Define styles with \tikzstyle{style name}=[options] or add to existing styles with \tikzstyle{style name}+=[options].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Styles may invoke other styles, forming hierarchies—avoid cyclic dependencies. Redefining an existing style silently replaces it. You can also set styles via the set style option inside a tikzpicture. Example: help lines style for background grids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate syntax general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinates are positions on the canvas given in round parentheses; general syntax is ([(options)](coordinate specification)). The coordinate specification uses one of many coordinate systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can explicitly select a coordinate system using name cs:key=value or use implicit special syntaxes for common systems (e.g., (30:1cm) for polar). Options in brackets apply to that coordinate (mainly for transformations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canvas coordinate system (explicit and implicit forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: canvas cs uses x=(dimension) and y=(dimension) to set distances from origin. Implicit form uses two dimensions separated by a comma, e.g., (1cm,1.5cm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can use expressions like 1cm+2pt as calc is available. Examples show \fill (canvas cs:x=1cm,y=1.5cm) circle (2pt) and implicit (1cm,1.5cm).

rubrics_metrics.name: xyz coordinate system
rubrics_metrics.description: xyz cs allows specifying a point as multiples of three vectors (x-, y-, z-vectors). Use x=, y=, z= factors. Implicit form uses two or three comma-separated factors (not dimensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default x-vector is 1cm right, y-vector 1cm up; z-vector default as specified. Useful for 3D-like coordinates; examples show drawing unit x,y,z vectors and using (0,0,1) style implicit coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: canvas polar coordinate system (angle/radius, implicit colon syntax)
rubrics_metrics.description: canvas polar cs: specify angle=(degrees) and radius=(dimension) to get the point at that radius from origin at the given angle. Implicit form is (angle:radius), e.g., (30:1cm). x radius and y radius allow ellipses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Angle must be in degrees (range recommended -360..720). Implicit angle words (up, down, left, right, north, south, etc.) are supported. Use x radius and y radius to specify elliptical radii.

rubrics_metrics.name: xyz polar / xy polar coordinate systems
rubrics_metrics.description: xyz polar interprets angle and radius in the current xy-coordinate system (angles measured relative to x-vector and y-vector); options: angle=(degrees), radius=(factor), x radius, y radius. xy polar is an alias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: radius is a multiplicative factor of the x/y vectors (no unit in implicit form). Use when the x/y basis has been modified (e.g., x={(0cm,1cm)}, y={(-1cm,0cm)}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Barycentric coordinate system
rubrics_metrics.description: barycentric cs: a coordinate is given as a comma-separated list of node-name=number pairs; the coordinate is the weighted average of the specified node centers: (α1 v1 + ... + αn vn)/(α1 + ... + αn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include spaces before/after the node name in the list. Currently you cannot specify anchors for nodes here (must create coordinates at anchors separately). Useful for combining positions of named nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Node coordinate system (node cs / implicit node syntax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use node cs:name=(node name), anchor=(anchor), angle=(degrees) to reference specific points inside/on a node; implicit syntax (a), (a.north) or (a.10) is supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither anchor nor angle is given TikZ will attempt to compute a reasonable border position automatically for line-to (--), |- and -|, and curve-to (...) operations; otherwise the center is used. Automatic computation may fail; give explicit anchors/angles if needed. Relative coordinates with automatic anchors: relative coords are computed relative to the node center, not the border point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection coordinate system
rubrics_metrics.description: intersection cs specifies the intersection of two lines by providing first line={(p1)--(p2)} and second line={(q1)--(q2)}; the coordinate is the intersection of these two lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must write -- between coordinates (special syntax; does not add to path). If the lines do not meet or are identical an arithmetic overflow error will result. Implicit form: (intersection of A--B and 1,2--3,0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpendicular coordinate system / p |- q syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Perpendicular coordinate system specifies intersection of a horizontal line through one coordinate and a vertical line through another: options horizontal line through=(coord), vertical line through=(coord). Implicit syntax is (p |- q) or (q -| p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces the coordinate at the vertical of p and horizontal of q (or vice versa). Useful for drawing a line up to some point on a vertical or horizontal line; examples show arrows to (p1 |- xline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining new coordinate systems
rubrics_metrics.description: \tikzdeclarecoordinatesystem{name}{code} declares a new coordinate system name that can be used as (name cs:arguments). The code receives the arguments as #1 and must set \pgf@x and \pgf@y to the canvas coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parsing the arguments with key-value syntax is customary but not required. You can create aliases with \tikzaliascoordinatesystem{new}{old}. Examples include a cylindrical coordinate system defined with keys angle/radius/z and using \pgfpointpolarxy and \pgfpointxyz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative and incremental coordinates (+ and ++)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefix coordinates with ++ to make them relative and update the current point (e.g., ++(1cm,0)). Use + to make a relative coordinate that does not update the current point (multiple points relative to the same initial point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rule for Bézier curve control points: a relative first control point is relative to the beginning of the curve; a relative second control point is relative to the end of the curve; a relative end point is relative to the start of the curve. This helps to control incoming/outgoing directions of curves. Use ++ for local sequences and + when you want multiple offsets from the same base point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path specification syntax and local options
rubrics_metrics.description: \path specification; a path is a stream of path operations (line-to --, curve-to, etc.). At any point where a path operation is expected you may give graphic options in brackets; these options are local to that point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many options apply to the whole path and cannot be scoped to a segment. Node specifications within the path take local options applying only to the node. The \path command is only available inside tikzpicture.
